expectedText:
NOTICE TO EMPLOYEE AS TO CHANGE IN RELATIONSHIP
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · Acme, Inc.

NOTICE OF CHANGE IN RELATIONSHIP
This notice is given to Jordan Alex Lee by Acme, Inc. in connection with a change in Jordan Alex Lee's employment relationship with Acme, Inc., effective September 1, 2026.

THE EDD PAMPHLET REQUIREMENT
California law requires every employer to supply each individual, at the time that individual becomes unemployed, with copies of printed (or, if the individual has opted in, electronic) statements or materials relating to unemployment benefit claims, in the form prescribed by the Employment Development Department's own regulations. The EDD's own guidance identifies the pamphlet employers are expected to distribute for this purpose as "For Your Benefit: California's Programs for the Unemployed" (EDD form DE 2320), describing it as something employers "must give each employee" when needed. The statute itself does not name a specific form number; the pamphlet's content, layout, and identifying number come from the EDD's implementing regulations and published guidance, not from the statutory text quoted below.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "Each employer shall, pursuant to authorized regulations, supply each individual at the time they become unemployed with copies of printed statements or materials relating to claims for benefits, or if the individual opts into receipt of electronic statements or materials, electronic statements or materials relating to claims for benefits. ... Printed statements shall be supplied by the director to each employer without cost to them."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089(b), (d) (California Legislative Information text), California Unemployment Insurance Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&division=1.&title=&part=1.&chapter=4.&article=6.)
  "Employee Benefit Rights You must give each employee the following when needed: For Your Benefit: California’s Programs for the Unemployed (DE 2320) (PDF): Information on UI, DI, PFL, and job service benefits."
  — Employment Development Department, "Required Notices and Pamphlets" (state agency guidance page), California EDD, Payroll Taxes – Required Notices and Pamphlets (https://edd.ca.gov/en/Payroll_Taxes/required_notices_and_pamphlets)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute (California Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089), used as real evidence that a state can require this kind of separation-time notice — not a claim about which state's law governs a given employer or employee. The statutory text is the primary source; the EDD webpage cited below is the agency's own administrative guidance identifying the DE 2320 pamphlet by name, and is offered as a second, independent confirmation that this pamphlet requirement is real and current — not as a restatement of the statute's own text, which does not use the phrase "DE 2320" or "For Your Benefit." The current version of § 1089 quoted here was amended effective January 1, 2024, and by its own terms sunsets on January 1, 2029, when a differently-numbered successor version (added by the same 2023 legislation) becomes operative; this document reflects the version in effect as of the checked date above.

THE SEPARATE "CHANGE IN RELATIONSHIP" NOTICE DUTY
The same statute imposes a second, distinct duty: an employer must immediately notify each employee of any change in that employee's relationship with the employer. The EDD's own guidance describes this as applying when an employee is fired, laid off, is taking a leave of absence, or otherwise has a change in job status, and states that written notice is required and a copy should be kept for the employer's records — while also identifying situations the agency treats as not requiring this written notice, including a voluntary quit, a promotion, a demotion, or work stopped because of a trade dispute.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "Each employer shall immediately notify each employee of any change in the employee’s relationship with that employer."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089(c) (California Legislative Information text), California Unemployment Insurance Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&division=1.&title=&part=1.&chapter=4.&article=6.)
  "Change in Employment You must immediately give written notice to employees if they are fired, laid off, taking a leave of absence, or if their job status changes. You should keep a copy for your records. This sample notice (PDF) meets the minimum requirements. You don't need to give written notice for a: Voluntary quit. Promotion Demotion Work stopped due to a trade dispute."
  — Employment Development Department, "Required Notices and Pamphlets" (state agency guidance page), California EDD, Payroll Taxes – Required Notices and Pamphlets (https://edd.ca.gov/en/Payroll_Taxes/required_notices_and_pamphlets)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute (California Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089(c)), used as real evidence that a change-in-relationship notice duty distinct from the benefits pamphlet exists — not a claim about which state's law governs a given separation. The statutory text itself is a single short sentence; the specific list of covered triggers (fired, laid off, leave of absence, job-status change) and excluded triggers (voluntary quit, promotion, demotion, trade-dispute work stoppage) comes from the EDD's own published guidance interpreting that sentence, not from additional statutory language, so it is offered as the agency's own administrative gloss rather than as a second independent statutory source. That same EDD guidance page links to the agency's own sample notice, titled "Notice to Employee as to Change in Relationship," as a form that "meets the minimum requirements" — confirming this document's subject matter tracks a real, currently-published EDD form, though this document does not reproduce that form's content.

NO EMPLOYER-SIZE THRESHOLD, AND NOT THE HIRING-TIME NOTICE
Unlike some other workplace notice laws, the statute described above applies to "each employer" without stating any minimum headcount, number of locations, or size of workforce reduction as a precondition. It is also a separate requirement from the notice California employers must give most new non-exempt hires at the start of employment describing pay rate, payday, and related information — that hiring-time notice is required under a different statute and is not addressed in this document.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "Each employer shall post and maintain, in places readily accessible to individuals in the employer’s service, printed statements concerning benefit rights and other matters as may be prescribed by authorized regulations. (b) Each employer shall, pursuant to authorized regulations, supply each individual at the time they become unemployed with copies of printed statements or materials relating to claims for benefits..."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089(a)-(b) (California Legislative Information text), California Unemployment Insurance Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&division=1.&title=&part=1.&chapter=4.&article=6.)
  "At the time of hiring, an employer shall provide to each employee a written notice, in the language the employer normally uses to communicate employment-related information to the employee, containing the following information..."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 2810.5(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=2810.5.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute (California Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089), used as real evidence that this particular notice duty is not conditioned on employer size — not a claim about which state's law governs a given employer. This clause states what the statute's text does and does not say; it does not independently confirm that no regulation or later enactment has added a size threshold not visible in the statutory text itself, though none was found. The hire-time notice referenced for contrast (Labor Code § 2810.5) is cited here only to distinguish it from the separation-time notice this document covers; this document does not address the hire-time notice's own content or requirements.

CONSEQUENCE OF NON-COMPLIANCE
The statute makes an employer's failure to comply with these notice duties a misdemeanor. That consequence is written directly into the same statutory section as the notice duties themselves, rather than into a separate penalty provision.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-01]
  "Failure to comply with this section by an employer shall constitute a misdemeanor."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089(g) (California Legislative Information text), California Unemployment Insurance Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&division=1.&title=&part=1.&chapter=4.&article=6.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute (California Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089(g)), used as real evidence that a compliance consequence exists — not a claim about which state's law governs a given employer. A separate statute this document's drafter initially expected to find a penalty in, Unemployment Insurance Code § 1142, was checked directly and does not impose a penalty for failing to give this notice or pamphlet at all: on its face, § 1142 penalizes an employer, or an employer's employee, officer, or agent, for willfully making a false statement or willfully failing to report a material fact when submitting facts about a claimant's termination for benefit-eligibility purposes under other, specifically enumerated sections — a different kind of misconduct entirely. This clause does not rely on § 1142, and no other provision imposing an additional civil penalty specifically for a violation of § 1089's notice duties was found in that section or the surrounding article; the misdemeanor language quoted above is the only compliance consequence this document verified. This clause cites a single statutory subsection (§ 1089(g)); no additional independent source was found for this.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Acme, Inc. is providing this notice, along with a copy of the EDD's "For Your Benefit" pamphlet (or an EDD-approved equivalent), to Jordan Alex Lee in connection with the change described above. This document describes the legal requirement to provide that pamphlet; it is not a substitute for the pamphlet itself, which Acme, Inc. must obtain separately from the EDD or its own authorized source.

Please sign below to acknowledge receipt of this notice and the accompanying pamphlet.

Employee: Jordan Alex Lee
Date: _______________
